SPECIFICATION FOR LAYING BATTERY CAGES FOR POULTRY
0.
0.1 This Indian

FOREWO

RD

Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 23 December 1974, after the draft finalized by the Animal Housing and Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Laying battery cages for keeping poultry are now gaining popularity. The cages consist of up to 3 tiers with a view to accommodating more birds in a given area. It also facilitates easier culling either due to sickness or low productivity of birds. These cages also ensure the production of clean eggs with minimum of care and attention and uniform exposure of flock to light and fresh air, thereby greatly reducing the incidence of vices like egg eating, feather picking and cannibalism. 0.3 Laying battery cages are manufactured in various shapes and sizes and their quality differs from manufacturer to manufacturer. However, the types of cages that are generally in vogue are: a) b) c) Single tier cages, one above the other with are placed in step deck Cages with more than one tier vertically intervening dropping tray, and Californian arrangement. type cages where the tiers

0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised).

IS : 7518 - 1974 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes materials and constructional laying battery cages for poultry. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply. 2.1 Laying Battery Cage -The space enclosed on all sides either for housing of individual bird or ~group of birds (not exceeding 5) with the provision for feeding, watering and removal of droppings. 2.2 Tier 3. 5.1.1 The height of the cage shall be 375 mm at the rear and 425 mm at the front. 6

IS : 7518 - I974 5.2 Frame - In Type B cages, the frame comprising four corner posts and connecting horizontal members at the top and the bottom should be of angle iron (see Table 1). 5.2.1 Depending angle iron supports on the length of the cage, it may be necessary at an interval of I.5 metres. to provide

5.3 Body and Floor - The mesh of the floor and the body (side) shall be not more than 25 x 75 mm. The wire mesh shall be stretched to avoid sagging and be securely fixed. 5.4 Projection - For facilitating the collection of eggs, the floor of the cage shall have a slope of 50 mm and there shall be a gap of 50 mm between the bottom of the front side and the floor so that the eggs automatically roll out of the cage. The end of the floor shall be extended by 225 mm in the front of which 75 mm should be curved to hold the eggs. Alternatively, the end of the floor may be extended by 150 mm in the front, of which 50 mm should be curved and a polyethylene or plastic lining about 25 mm below the top of the projection curve should be provided to safeguard against the eggs striking right on the edge of the curve resulting in cracks or possible breakages. 5.5 Dropping Tray - In Type B cages, below the floor, there shall be a removeable tray having edge of 20 mm on all sides for collecting the droppings. In the front of the dropping tray, a handle shall be provided. These trays may be one for each cage or preferably a long tray not exceeding 750 mm in length and resting on angle iron frames may be provided for economizing the operation. The distance between the front curvature of the floor of the cage and the dropping tray shall be minimum 75 mm. 5.6 Feed and Water Troughs - Each tier of cages shall be provided The length of the troughs shall be with one water and one feed trough. equal to the length of the tier, with a view to providing common watering and feeding facilities. These troughs shall be fixed outside. In case of Type A and Type B cages, the troughs may be fixed either in the front The troughs shall rest on welded hooks. or in the back. The dimensions and lip of the troughs are illustrated in Fig. 3. The feed troughs should be at a height of 125 mm from the floor and the water trough at the height If desired by the purchaser, the water and the feed troughs of 250 mm. may be provided separately with each cage. 5.7 Doors-The doors shall be provided at the front of the cage and should have two parallel vertical wires welded on the top and at the bottom (see Fig. 4). 5.8 Legs - In case of Type B cages, an angle iron support, extending 250 mm below the lower side of the dropping tray shall be provided to act as legs. 7

5.9 The tiered laying battery cages shall be so constructed as to be stable and not turn over with full load of the birds. 5.10 Types A and C cages, if hung from the roof, should have a single point fixed hanger to avoid oscillation. The hanger may have slots to adjust the heighi of the cage from the ground. . 6. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH

6.1 The frame joints shall be properly welded and finished smooth. 6.2 For protection against rusting and corrosion, the iron steel parts shall be suitably protected. 7. MARKING AND PACKING

7.1 Marking-Each laying battery cage shall be legibly and indelibly marked on its outer surface with the following particulars: a) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark, b) Manufacturer's model or type reference, c) Year of manufacture, 8

d) Any essential operating instructions, e) Number of birds per cage. 7.1.1 Mark.

Each laying cage may also be marked with the IS1 Certification

NOTE- The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations made The IS1 mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the thereunder. assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers Institution. or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards

7.2 Packing - Laying battery cages shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 8. TESTS
8.1 Visual Examination and Inspection - Each laying cage shall be examined and inspected for general construction, materials (see 4) and other requirements (see 5). There shall be no signs of rusting, sagging, deformation and loosening of joints.
